title: Development and Characterization of Hyaluronic Acid Graft-Modified Polydopamine Nanoparticles for Antibacterial Studies
content: The problem of antibiotic abuse and drug resistance is becoming more and more serious. in recent years, polydopamine (PDA) nanoparticles have been recognized as a potential antimicrobial material for photothermal therapy (PTT) due to their excellent photothermal conversion efficiency and unique antimicrobial ability.PDA is capable of rapidly converting light energy into heat energy under near-infrared (NIR) light irradiation to efficiently kill bacteria. In order to solve the problem of PDA's tendency to aggregate and precipitate, this study improved its stability by grafting hyaluronic acid (HA) on the surface of PDA. Using dopamine and hyaluronic acid as raw materials, hyaluronic acid (HA) was grafted onto polydopamine (PDA) nanoparticles by self-polymerization and Michael addition reactions under alkaline conditions to obtain PDA-HA modified nanoparticles. We confirmed the successful grafting of hyaluronic acid by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), nuclear magnetic hydrogen spectrometry (¹H NMR), Raman spectroscopy (Raman) analysis and other test methods. Near-infrared performance experiments showed that the temperature of PDA-HA solution increased rapidly under near-infrared light irradiation, demonstrating excellent photothermal conversion performance. In vitro antimicrobial experiments showed that PDA-HA had excellent antimicrobial effects against Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and Escherichia coli (E. coli), and the antimicrobial rate was 100% under near-infrared light irradiation. The material is simple to prepare and provides a new idea for developing new antibacterial materials, which is of great clinical significance for the treatment of bacterial infections.
